brief: The owner preferred OIDC only unless there was a good reason to keep passwords.
tradeoff: Households that turn passwords off: no typing a password into an app; new devices sign in by Quick Connect, and an app without it cannot sign in.
entry: Password sign-in stays. With no provider it is on. Once a provider is declared it is off for everyone but the configured adminUser (break-glass), unless passwordSignIn is true. Issued tokens survive the switch. The refusal is D-020's 403, logged with its reason. JS-039 gains these criteria; JS-033, JS-060, JS-180, JS-179 and the order are unchanged. OIDC only would make a provider a required service against goal 5, leave no way to make the first admin, and no first sign-in without a shipped web client.
serves: PRODUCT.md goals 3 and 5; 'Signing in is easy and safe'.
